text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: GPU pool surge in us-west1 (hotpath) — p95 latency spike, rising 429s on hosted tier. Auto-scaler reports failed transitions. Root cause unknown, oncall please respond.
erin_oncall: I'm on it. Observing alert: generated 429s ~ 06:12 UTC, queue growth > 3k, hotpool usage at 100%. Which customers hit?
maya_support: seeing increased tickets for slow responses from LogiCorp and two other mid-market tenants. Support triage says repeated retries leading to client-side backoffs.
sam_sre: I'm pulling autoscaler logs. Quick summary: autoscaler tried to acquire GPU slots but hit pool_limit + lock contention when applying token-window resync. Looks like multiple concurrent scale operations timed out.
jules_runtime: tagging in — also seeing ratepolicy config change pushed earlier this morning that modified token bucket refill rate for hosted->standard tier. Could be starving token refill under burst.
erin_oncall: @sam_sre @jules_runtime priority: stabilize customer-facing traffic, then fix auto-scale deadlock. Any hotfix we can do?
sam_sre: two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase hotpath pool cap (manual bump), 2) enable fallback routing to dedicated-pool for low-priority requests. I can do 1 if eng approves.
natalie_eng: approving manual bump for emergency only. Which command?
sam_sre: runbook: autoscale manual bump: ```sh
rctl pool resize --pool hotpath-us-west1 --target-instances 24 --reason "incident 1689500000 manual bump"
```
That should help drain queue while we diagnose.
jules_runtime: also recommend loosening tier tokenbucket thresholds to avoid 429s while scaling is slow. Current config (deployed 03:05) sets refill_ms=60000, burst=100 -> granular clients starve at high concurrency. Temporarily set refill_ms=20000, burst=300 for hosted-standard.
erin_oncall: @deploy-bot can we toggle tokenbucket config via feature flag? We need an atomic rollback too.
deploy-bot: triggered rollout: featureflag/tokenbucket-relax -> canary 1 -> awaiting approval.
maya_support: heads up — customers seeing 429s get a standard message; we pushed a status page note at 06:20 UTC.
sam_sre: log dump from autoscaler coordinator (truncated): ```
[06:11:54] autoscaler: requestScale({pool:hotpath-us-west1, want:24}) -> lock timeout
[06:12:01] orchestrator: queue_len=3124, in_flight=128, gpu_util=100%
[06:12:07] tokenwindow: failed_resync tenant=hosted refid=cfg-2023-07-18 err=optimistic-lock
[06:12:13] autoscaler: abort scale, schedule retry backoff=30s
```
jules_runtime: that optimistic-lock suggests concurrent config writes — probably the tokenbucket change deploy collided with autoscaler state sync. Need to reconcile.
erin_oncall: status update: I'm executing manual bump (sam, help me validate metrics after).
sam_sre: acknowledged, watching metrics.
[06:18 UTC] erin_oncall: executed resize command. Pool target moved to 24. Not seeing immediate new instances join; kube events show init latency ~ 90s per node.
jules_runtime: while nodes join, I pushed tokenbucket relax flag to canary 1. Will monitor 429 rate.
[06:22 UTC] deploy-bot: featureflag/tokenbucket-relax canary 1 -> success on 2 hosts.
sam_sre: 429 rate dropped from 18% -> 8% in 2m. queue length trending down: 3124 -> 1100. p95 latency from 28s -> 12s.
maya_support: stitching messages to affected customers, offering temporary retry guidance. Major customer LogiCorp flagged as high impact; they got repeated 429s for ~10 minutes.
nerin_oncall: I'm going to failover slow tenants to dedicated-pool for remaining backlog. @natalie_eng authorize?
natalie_eng: yep, go ahead. Use `routefix` playbook.
jules_runtime: routefix snippet: ```yaml
- match: path_prefix: /v1/generate
  tier: hosted
  action: reroute: dedicated-pool-us-west1
  conditions: low_priority=true
```
sam_sre: executed selective reroute for low_priority flag. After reroute queue back to ~200, p95 ~5s for routed traffic.
nerin_oncall: customer impact summary (so far): 12 tenants with elevated errors, 3 high-priority (LogiCorp, DataGraph, FinOps). No data loss, only transient 429s and higher latencies. Support escalations: 5 open tickets.
maya_support: LogiCorp CS rep called; CRM ticket #INC-985. They've accepted the mitigation and want a postmortem.
sam_sre: root cause hypothesis: concurrent config change reduced token refill rate while autoscaler had a lock contention bug. Combined effects: tokenbucket starvation + autoscale fail -> queue growth -> global thinning -> 429s.
jules_runtime: next steps: (1) revert the offending tokenbucket config change in staging and run canary tests, (2) patch autoscaler lock logic to avoid abort on optimistic-lock (PR in progress), (3) add preflight check to refuse config writes when scale operations in progress.
erin_oncall: I've recorded mitigation timeline in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1689500000 (draft).
sam_sre: follow-up actions scheduled: backfill automation to detect tokenbucket-change+autoscale race, add metric alert for token-refill-rate vs queue-growth correlation.
jules_runtime: also add a soft-fail fallback that reroutes to cheaper model variant when p95 > 10s and queue > 500. Prevents 429 storms.
maya_support: will notify affected customers and schedule syncs. LogiCorp wants a technical contact for postmortem; assign to jules_runtime.
nerin_oncall: handoff: I'll be oncall for the next 30m to watch for regression, then hand to @sam_sre for follow-up tasks. If anything spikes > 10% errors reopen page.
sam_sre: taking post-incident followups. Filing a Jira: INFRA-4321 with timeline and action items.
[07:10 UTC] erin_oncall: incident declared RESOLVED — 429 rate back to baseline, pool healthy, ticket count decreasing. Closing thread once postmortem drafted. :thumbsup:
